findings.title: Federated recovery codes stored as raw plaintext
findings.body: In CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential the raw codes from the form (generatedCodes) are serialized to JSON and sent to user storage via UserCredentialModel, while the local-DB path stores RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel which contains hashed codes. External storage therefore receives and persists usable plaintext recovery codes, whereas local storage persists hashes. Anyone with read access to the federated store can impersonate the user.

findings.title: Federated recovery-code validation allows infinite reuse
findings.body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse())) and never marks the used code as consumed. The local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider burns a code on successful isValid and tracks allCodesUsed. The federated path therefore leaves all codes valid forever, so one leaked code can be replayed indefinitely and exhaustion is never detected.

findings.title: getCredentials loses ID and NPEs on unknown user
findings.body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials, myUser is dereferenced without a null check, so lookup of a user not in the map throws NullPointerException. When present, the method rebuilds the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) from credentialData/createdDate only, discarding the stored CredentialModel id set in updateCredential. Every call returns a different random id, so callers that use the id for removal or display (e.g. removeStoredCredentialById) can never match the persisted credential.

findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery credential never removed
findings.body: After successful validation the code loads the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential which prefers federated credentials, then unconditionally calls credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById when allCodesUsed(). removeStoredCredentialById only deletes local Keycloak-DB credentials. A federated credential is therefore never cleaned up, and the test provider's disableCredentialType does not even support the recovery type, leaving an exhausted credential in external storage.

findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get causes 500 when credential missing
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) then immediately credentialModelOpt.get() without checking isPresent, followed by getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). If the credential was just consumed, removed, or the user only has the other storage type in a race, this throws NoSuchElementException and produces a 500 during login-form rendering instead of a handled error or re-setup.
